An Argentine footballer, Abel Núñez, has died days after suffering a head injury during a match while representing Ezeiza Football Club. The club announced his death in a statement released on Sunday, expressing sadness over the loss of the young player, who had undergone surgery after the incident. “After suffering a hard blow during a match, proudly wearing our Ezeiza shirt, we deeply regret his departure,” the club said. It added, “Today football is in the background. We are overwhelmed by the pain of saying goodbye to a colleague, a young man full of dreams and hopes, who was part of our family.” Reports said Núñez was playing for Ezeiza’s fifth-division team in the Argentine Football Association’s Juveniles C Copa de Plata competition when he was struck in the head by a ball during a match against Deportivo Muñiz. The incident reportedly occurred at Club Atlético La Sonia in José C. Paz, where Núñez collapsed on the pitch and received immediate medical attention before being taken to hospital for surgery. Days before announcing his death, Ezeiza had appealed to its community to support the player as he underwent treatment following the injury. In an earlier statement, the club said Núñez had suffered a serious blow to the head that required surgery, urging players, families, coaches and supporters to join in prayers for his recovery. Following his death, the club extended its condolences to his family, friends, teammates and loved ones, saying he would always remain part of its family. Christabel Ndoeche
